input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Governing law is Arizona, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails both the preferred and fallback positions on a material term. There is also no venue provision, and Section 19 imposes mandatory binding arbitration under private rules with confirmation in the district of the losing party's residence — the arbitration is domestic rather than seated abroad, so this is not walk-away territory, but the forum does not track any accepted jurisdiction. We moved the governing law to New York with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County (preferred position) and seated any arbitration in New York County so the forum matches; Delaware, California, or England and Wales with London courts remain acceptable fallbacks.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Arizona to New York and add exclusive New York County venue; seat any arbitration in New York County.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law from Arizona to New York and added exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our standard position; Delaware, California, or England and Wales (London courts) are acceptable alternatives. We have also seated any arbitration in New York County so the dispute forum matches the governing law.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

ops.newText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration seated in New York County, New York pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com)
